creatures.name: Monarchwing
creatures.habitat: Great Plains, Meadows & Oyamel Fir Forests
creatures.education: Monarch butterflies complete one of the greatest migrations on Earth, flying up to 3,000 miles from Canada to Mexico! They have a magnetic compass in their brains and use the angle of the sun to navigate. Milkweed makes them toxic to birds, and their bright orange color is a warning sign!
creatures.exploration_trait: Wayfinder Compass (Points the player toward regional waypoints and migratory trails on the minimap).
creatures.visual_notes: Radiant stained-glass orange wings with black borders and white polka dots along wing edges.

creatures.name: Fireglow
creatures.habitat: Damp Meadows, Forest Margins & Stream Edges
creatures.education: Fireflies are actually beetles that produce 100% efficient cold light—no energy is lost as heat! Males fly in the warm summer twilight making distinctive 'J'-shaped flashes of yellow-green light to signal females resting in the grass below.
creatures.exploration_trait: Twilight Lantern (Illuminates campsites and dark paths with warm, soothing bioluminescent light).
creatures.visual_notes: Sleek dark brown beetle with a rose-red neck shield and an abdomen glowing with warm emerald-gold fire.

creatures.name: Brood-Thirteen
creatures.education: Periodical cicadas live underground for 13 or 17 prime-numbered years as nymphs before millions crawl out all at once! Scientists believe they use prime numbers so predators cannot sync their life cycles to them. When they emerge, their singing reaches 100 decibels!
creatures.exploration_trait: Prime Emergence (Unlocks dormant underground chambers that only open during cyclical game events).
creatures.visual_notes: Stout black body with glowing red jewel eyes and bright orange wing veins.

creatures.name: Honeypot-Cask
creatures.education: In the hot desert, honeypot ants serve as living storage barrels! Specialized worker ants called 'repletes' hang from the ceiling of underground burrows while other ants pump their bellies full of sweet nectar until they swell like golden grapes to feed the colony in droughts.
creatures.exploration_trait: Nectar Canteen (Stores emergency hydration and stamina syrups for long desert treks).
creatures.visual_notes: Translucent amber swollen abdomen resembling a glowing droplet of liquid honey suspended on six delicate legs.

creatures.name: Red-Harvester
creatures.education: Red harvester ants clear wide circular rings around their nests, clipping every blade of grass to prevent prairie fires from burning their home! They collect wild grass seeds and store them in dry underground granaries, helping spread native prairie plants.
creatures.exploration_trait: Granary Sifter (Collects wild cereal seeds and grains to supply homestead kitchens and seed banks).
creatures.visual_notes: Sturdy rust-red ant with heavy crushing mandibles and a bearded chin fringe used for basket-carrying seeds.

creatures.name: Hourglass
creatures.habitat: Dark Woodpiles, Rock Piles & Dry Culverts
creatures.education: The black widow's silk is pound-for-pound stronger than high-grade steel cable! While famous for the bright red hourglass on her belly, black widows are shy creatures that only bite in self-defense when squeezed. Their tangled webs are non-sticky but super springy.
creatures.exploration_trait: Steel-Silk Anchor (Spins ultra-durable suspension lines used for bridging narrow canyon crevasses).
creatures.visual_notes: Glossy porcelain-black bulbous abdomen stamped with a vivid crimson hourglass mark.

creatures.name: Desert-Blonde
creatures.education: Female Arizona blonde tarantulas can live for over 30 years! During summer monsoon rains, hundreds of roaming male tarantulas embark on an evening trek across desert highways looking for mates. They are calm, docile giants of the desert world.
creatures.exploration_trait: Burrow Cork (Seals underground entrance burrows with silk and soil to prevent desert storm flooding).
creatures.visual_notes: Plump velvety spider with a pale blonde-grey carapace, dark velvet abdomen, and copper leg hairs.

creatures.name: Bombus-Fuzz
creatures.diet: Pollen & Nectar of Native Prairie Flowers
creatures.education: Bumblebees practice 'buzz pollination'! They grab onto flowers (like tomatoes and blueberries) and vibrate their flight muscles at high frequency without flapping their wings. This acoustic buzz shakes pollen free that honeybees can't reach!
creatures.exploration_trait: Sonic Pollinate (Vibrates wild crop plants to increase agricultural harvest yields at the homestead).
creatures.visual_notes: Chubby, adorably fuzzy yellow-and-black striped body with velvety black head and shimmering translucent wings.

creatures.name: Dragonhunter
creatures.education: The dragonhunter is a giant clubtail dragonfly that hunts other dragonflies right out of the sky! In flight, its backward-curved legs form a barbed basket that scoops up flying prey at 30 miles per hour, making it an apex aerial insect predator.
creatures.exploration_trait: Interceptor Patrol (Scouts and neutralizes annoying swarm pests around player base camps).
creatures.visual_notes: Striking yellow-and-black striped thorax, massive emerald compound eyes, and a clubbed tail.

creatures.name: Lunawing
creatures.diet: Nutrient reserves from caterpillar days (adults don't eat!)
creatures.education: Luna moths have long twisted ribbon tails on their hind wings. When flying at night, the spinning tails bounce bat sonar waves away, tricking hungry bats into attacking the harmless feather tails instead of the moth's body!
creatures.exploration_trait: Sonar Deflector (Confuses cave-dwelling flying predators, causing their attacks to miss).
creatures.visual_notes: Luminous pale lime-green silk wings with maroon leading edges, four eyespots, and elegant twisted tail ribbons.

creatures.name: Hickory-Devil
creatures.education: The hickory horned devil looks like a tiny dragon! Growing up to six inches long, this caterpillar brandishes long orange-and-black curved horns on its head that make it look terrifying, but it is completely harmless and turns into a regal orange-and-yellow moth.
creatures.exploration_trait: Dragon Bluff (Frightens small predators away with its fierce horned posture).
creatures.visual_notes: Massive teal-green caterpillar adorned with formidable curved orange horns tipped with black spikes.

creatures.name: Wheel-Crest
creatures.education: The wheel bug gets its name from a strange cog-wheel crest on its back that looks like a miniature medieval armor cog! It has a curved beak that it plunges into garden pest caterpillars, injecting digestive juices to clean gardens of harmful pests.
creatures.exploration_trait: Cog Gear Mechanic (Interlocks its back crest with ancient mill gears to turn mechanical puzzles).
creatures.visual_notes: Slate-gray armored body crowned by a prominent semicircular cogwheel cog crest along its dorsal ridge.

creatures.name: Eyed-Clicker
creatures.education: This beetle has two huge velvety black 'false eyes' bordered in white on its chest! If a hungry woodpecker inspects the wood, the fake giant eyes startle the bird. If caught, the beetle clicks its chest spine to catapult three feet into the air!
creatures.exploration_trait: Spring Escape (Can launch itself upward to collect high floating collectibles from low ceilings).
creatures.visual_notes: Mottled salt-and-pepper armor plate featuring two giant velvety black false eyes circled in white.

creatures.name: Sand-Funnel
creatures.education: Antlion larvae are nicknamed 'doodlebugs' because of the meandering winding tracks they make in soft sand while searching for the perfect spot to dig their conical pits. They fling sand grains with precision to knock ants down into their jaws!
creatures.exploration_trait: Doodle Tracker (Draws guiding lines in loose soil showing the optimal route through sandy mazes).
creatures.visual_notes: Sandy stout larva with curved sickle mandibles, evolving into a delicate four-winged lace fly.

creatures.name: Velvet-Cow
creatures.habitat: Dry Pastures, Sandy Fields & Forest Edges
creatures.education: Known as the 'cow killer ant,' this creature can't actually kill a cow, but its sting is intensely painful! When threatened, it makes a high-pitched squeaking noise by rubbing segments of its abdomen together to warn everyone to back away.
creatures.exploration_trait: Stridulation Siren (Emits a sharp warning squeak that alerts companions to incoming stealth ambushers).
creatures.visual_notes: Plump wingless wasp blanketed in bright scarlet-orange plush velvet fur with contrasting velvet black.

creatures.name: Six-Spot
creatures.education: Tiger beetles run so fast that their eyes can't process light fast enough, causing them to go temporarily blind! They sprint in short supersonic bursts, stop for a split second to let their vision catch up, and then pounce on their prey with toothy jaws.
creatures.exploration_trait: Sprint Dash (Delivers brief bursts of high-speed overland sprint across trail surfaces).
creatures.visual_notes: Glittering metallic emerald-green shell spotted with six small ivory dots and white sickle jaws.

creatures.name: Hellgrammite
creatures.education: Dobsonfly larvae are called 'hellgrammites' and live under river rocks for up to five years, serving as clean-water indicators. Adult males have giant curved tusk pincers that look terrifying, but they are so long that they are too weak to pinch humans!
creatures.exploration_trait: Purity Sensor (Tests river water purity to locate pristine mineral springs and avoid toxic runoff).
creatures.visual_notes: Slate-gray lace wings spanning five inches with enormous sickle tusks arching from the male's head.

creatures.name: Bark-Stinger
creatures.habitat: Riparian Desert Washes & Tree Bark Crevices
creatures.education: The Arizona bark scorpion is the only scorpion in North America that can climb high into trees and vertical walls! It can survive being frozen solid in winter and thaws out completely fine in the spring sun, glowing vibrant neon turquoise under UV blacklight.
creatures.exploration_trait: Cryo-Thaw (Endures freezing environmental temperatures and revives without cold penalties).
creatures.visual_notes: Slender straw-yellow desert scorpion with delicate pincers and an elegant curved tail that curls horizontally.

creatures.name: Giant-Silk
creatures.diet: Stored energy from oak/maple leaf eating caterpillar
creatures.education: Named after Polyphemus, the giant one-eyed Cyclops from Greek mythology, this silk moth has huge translucent circular eyespots on its hind wings that look like giant mammalian eyes, designed to startle songbirds that try to peck it.
creatures.exploration_trait: Cyclops Glare (Stuns approaching aerial enemies for a few seconds upon surprise encounter).
creatures.visual_notes: Broad velvety ochre-tan wings spanning six inches with prominent blue-and-yellow rimmed circular eyespots.

creatures.name: Stink-Shield
creatures.education: Stink bugs are shaped like medieval shields! When threatened, specialized scent glands between their legs release a pungent defensive cocktail of chemicals that smells like foul cilantro, preventing birds and spiders from eating them.
creatures.exploration_trait: Pungent Perimeter (Deploys an odor boundary that prevents common garden pests from nibbling crops).
creatures.visual_notes: Shield-shaped bronze-brown carapace with alternating white and black bands along the abdominal rim.

creatures.name: Yellow-Stripe
creatures.education: Yellowjackets build intricate multi-layered paper palaces underground! They chew weathered gray wood fibers and mix them with saliva to create papier-mâché nests that can house thousands of industrious workers.
creatures.exploration_trait: Paper Craft (Harvests fine pulp fibers used to manufacture map scrolls, parchment, and blueprints).
creatures.visual_notes: Sharp black-and-canary yellow striped body with clear folded wings and an aggressive forward posture.

creatures.name: Lady-Nine
creatures.education: A single nine-spotted ladybug can gobble up over 5,000 crop-destroying aphids in its lifetime! If picked up by a predator, it oozes a yellow droplet of bitter fluid from its knee joints ('reflex bleeding') to teach the predator that ladybugs taste foul.
creatures.exploration_trait: Aphid Banisher (Clears infested farm crops and plant gardens of parasitic blights and pests).
creatures.visual_notes: Polished domed scarlet wing covers marked with exactly nine neat black dots and white cheek patches.

creatures.name: Cutter-Bee
creatures.education: Unlike honeybees that carry pollen in baskets on their legs, leafcutter bees carry pollen on a dense brush of hairs on the bottom of their belly called a 'scopa'! They cut neat circles out of rose leaves to wallpaper their baby nursery tubes.
creatures.exploration_trait: Belly-Brush Pollen (Collects mass botanical pollen used in potion brewing and fertilizer compounding).
creatures.visual_notes: Compact charcoal-gray bee with white hair bands and a vibrant golden brush of pollen on its underbelly.

creatures.name: Organ-Dauber
creatures.education: This gentle solitary wasp sculpts long parallel mud tubes that look like the pipes of a church organ! Male mud daubers are devoted home guardians: while the female flies to fetch wet clay, the male stands guard at the tube entrance against parasitic flies.
creatures.exploration_trait: Clay Pipe Masonry (Builds durable acoustic chime tubes that sound alarms when enemies approach).
creatures.visual_notes: Elongated metallic blue-black wasp with milky white back feet and rhythmic vibrating wings.

creatures.name: Skater-Strider
creatures.habitat: Calm Lake Surfaces, Slow Rivers & Ponds
creatures.diet: Fallen Insects trapped in surface tension
creatures.education: Water striders walk on water using surface tension! Their long legs are covered in thousands of microscopic water-repellent hairs that trap tiny cushions of air. They literally slide across water like ice skaters without ever getting their feet wet!
creatures.exploration_trait: Surface Skater (Skates effortlessly across water surfaces to retrieve floating debris and seeds).
creatures.visual_notes: Slender dark brown insect with four long sprawling pontoon legs creating tiny dimples on the water.

creatures.name: Gila-Bead
creatures.education: The Gila monster's bumpy skin looks like intricate beaded Native American beadwork! It stores fat in its thick tail to survive months without food. Scientists studied its venom and developed life-saving medicine for human diabetes from a protein in its saliva!
creatures.exploration_trait: Beaded Armor (Grants natural resistance to blunt damage and searing desert heat).
creatures.visual_notes: Heavy-bodied lizard patterned with brilliant mosaic bands of pinkish-orange and jet black beaded scales.

creatures.name: Gator-King
creatures.education: Alligators are ecosystem engineers! During winter droughts, they dig deep mud depressions called 'alligator holes' that stay filled with water, saving thousands of fish, turtles, and wading birds until rains return. Male gators vibrate water on their backs during bellowing dances!
creatures.exploration_trait: Gator Hole Dredge (Digs emergency waterholes in dried-up wetland zones to restore aquatic life).
creatures.visual_notes: Massive black-armored reptile with a broad rounded snout, armored scutes, and powerful swimming tail.

creatures.name: Diamond-Rattle
creatures.habitat: Pine Flatwoods, Coastal Dunes & Palmetto Scrub
creatures.education: The eastern diamondback is the heaviest venomous snake in the Americas! Its rattle is made of interlocking rings of keratin (the same stuff as human fingernails). Every time it sheds its skin, it adds a new rattle ring that buzzes like a dry maraca!
creatures.exploration_trait: Rattle Ward (Rattles tail to scare away hostile territorial wildlife without initiating combat).
creatures.visual_notes: Heavy brown body marked with dark chocolate diamonds rimmed in cream and a straw-colored rattle tail.

creatures.name: Cottonmouth
creatures.education: The cottonmouth is the world's only semi-aquatic pit viper! When approached, it coils up, tilts its head back, and opens its mouth wide, displaying a snowy-white cottony mouth lining as a clear warning sign to back away.
creatures.exploration_trait: Bayou Swim (Swims buoyancy-stable through thick swamp duckweed and cypress knees).
creatures.visual_notes: Olive-brown dark-banded water serpent with a triangular head and startling snow-white inner mouth.

creatures.name: Copper-Coil
creatures.education: Copperheads have an hourglass camouflage pattern that blends in so perfectly with fallen autumn oak leaves that people can step right beside them without seeing them! Baby copperheads have a bright sulfur-yellow tail tip that they wiggle like a worm to lure frogs.
creatures.exploration_trait: Leaf-Litter Veil (Grants the player total stealth in fallen autumn leaf terrain).
creatures.visual_notes: Copper-red head with a body patterned in hourglass bands of rich chestnut and salmon-tan.

creatures.name: Bull-Bellow
creatures.habitat: Warm Lakes, Ponds, Marshes & Farm Swamps
creatures.diet: Insects, Crayfish, Fish, Small Snakes, Mice
creatures.education: The American bullfrog is the largest frog in North America! Its deep booming call sounds like a roaring bull, which gave it its name. They don't sleep in the traditional sense—experiments showed they remain alert and responsive day and night!
creatures.exploration_trait: Deep Bog Vault (Leaps across wide marsh ponds and lands on floating lily pads safely).
creatures.visual_notes: Heavy olive-green frog with a yellow throat, massive gold-rimmed eardrums (tympana), and powerful legs.

creatures.name: Hellbender
creatures.education: The hellbender is a giant aquatic salamander that can grow over two feet long! Nicknamed the 'snot otter,' it is completely covered in loose wrinkly skin folds that absorb oxygen directly from cold mountain stream water without using its lungs!
creatures.exploration_trait: Riffle Crevice (Squeezes beneath heavy riverbed flagstones to locate underwater relics).
creatures.visual_notes: Flat slate-brown salamander with loose frilly skin folds along its flanks, tiny eyes, and paddle tail.

creatures.name: Axolotl-Neoteny
creatures.education: Axolotls are nature's eternal babies! They exhibit 'neoteny,' meaning they keep their cute feathery baby gills and live in water their whole lives without growing up. They have miraculous regenerative powers—they can regrow lost limbs, tails, and even parts of their brain and heart!
creatures.exploration_trait: Miracle Regeneration (Passively accelerates the health and vitality recovery of party members).
creatures.visual_notes: Charming smiling amphibian with pink-frilled feathery external gills and a translucent paddle fin tail.

creatures.name: Alligator-Snap
creatures.habitat: Deep River Channels, Canals & Swamp Lakes
creatures.education: Weighing over 200 pounds, this is one of the heaviest freshwater turtles in the world! It lies motionless on the muddy riverbed with its mouth wide open, wiggling a fleshy bright pink worm-like lure on the tip of its tongue. When a curious fish swims in to eat the worm—SNAP!
creatures.exploration_trait: Worm Tongue Lure (Lures rare and elusive fish species directly to the riverbank for easy catching).
creatures.visual_notes: Prehistoric dragon-like shell with three spiked ridges, heavily keeled skin, hooked beak, and pink lure tongue.

creatures.name: Horned-Horny
creatures.education: Commonly called 'horny toads,' these are actually desert lizards! When cornered by a coyote or fox, the horned lizard can increase the blood pressure in its eye sockets and squirt a thin stream of foul-tasting blood from its eyes up to five feet away to repel the canine!
creatures.exploration_trait: Blood Squirt Ward (Repels predatory canids and wolves with an auto-defensive foul spray).
creatures.visual_notes: Flat rounded pancake body covered in sharp crown horns and fringed desert-camo scales.

creatures.name: Chuckwalla-Puff
creatures.education: When a predator approaches a chuckwalla, it scurries into a tight rock crevice and inhales deeply, puffing up its loose skin like a spiky balloon! Wedged so tightly into the rock, predators cannot pull it out no matter how hard they tug.
creatures.exploration_trait: Crevice Wedge (Can wedge itself into cracked stone arches to hold them open for the player).
creatures.visual_notes: Plump wrinkled pot-bellied desert lizard with rough charcoal skin and rusty orange highlights.

creatures.name: Common-Snap
creatures.education: Common snapping turtles can live for over a century! Unlike most turtles that pull their heads inside their shells when scared, the snapping turtle has a tiny belly shell, so it relies on its lightning-fast striking neck and powerful beak to defend itself on land.
creatures.exploration_trait: Root Sever (Snips thick underwater tree roots that tangle boat propellers and nets).
creatures.visual_notes: Rugged mud-stained carapace with saw-toothed tail crest and a formidable sharp hooked beak.

creatures.name: Box-Hinged
creatures.education: The box turtle has a hinged plastron (belly shell) that can close completely tight like a strong wooden chest! Once closed, not even a knife blade can slip inside. They love eating toxic wild mushrooms that are poisonous to humans without getting sick at all!
creatures.exploration_trait: Mushroom Forager (Safely identifies and collects rare culinary and medicinal forest fungi).
creatures.visual_notes: High domed shell painted in brilliant yellow-orange sunburst flares on chocolate-brown horn plates.

creatures.name: Rainbow-Trout
creatures.habitat: Cold Clear Mountain Rivers & Pacific Streams
creatures.education: Rainbow trout have a brilliant reddish-pink lateral stripe that shines like a rainbow in clear alpine waters! Some individuals migrate out to the open Pacific Ocean where they grow huge and silver (called steelheads) before leaping up waterfalls to return home.
creatures.exploration_trait: Waterfall Leap (Can leap up turbulent white-water rapids to access hidden alpine mountain lakes).
creatures.visual_notes: Streamlined silver-olive body sprinkled with black speckles and an iridescent fiery pink lateral band.

creatures.name: Alligator-Gar
creatures.habitat: Slow Rivers, Bayous & Oxbow Lakes of the South
creatures.diet: Fish, Blue Crabs, Waterfowl, Small Turtles
creatures.education: The alligator gar is a prehistoric giant that swam alongside the dinosaurs 100 million years ago! It can grow up to 10 feet long and is covered in diamond-shaped ganoid scales so hard and enamel-covered that Native Americans used them as arrowheads!
creatures.exploration_trait: Ganoid Armor (Provides diamond-scale plating used to craft puncture-proof wilderness armor).
creatures.visual_notes: Colossal torpedo-shaped river titan with an alligator-like broad snout and interlocking enamel scale armor.

creatures.name: Bald-Eagle
creatures.habitat: Lakes, Coastal Bays & Broad River Valleys
creatures.education: The bald eagle builds the largest bird nests in the world! A single pair will add sticks to the same nest year after year; the largest recorded eagle nest was 10 feet wide, 20 feet deep, and weighed nearly three tons! Their eyesight is four times sharper than a human's.
creatures.exploration_trait: Apex Survey (Removes vast fog-of-war areas from the region map from high mountain perches).
creatures.visual_notes: Dark brown plumage with snowy-white head and tail, piercing yellow eyes, and massive hooked yellow bill.

creatures.name: Golden-Eagle
creatures.education: The golden eagle is one of the fastest and fiercest aerial hunters in the northern hemisphere! Diving at over 200 miles per hour, they use their immense talons to hunt prey on steep mountain cliffs and can easily lift prey heavier than themselves.
creatures.exploration_trait: Thermal Lift (Creates powerful aerial updrafts that carry flying mounts across alpine gaps).
creatures.visual_notes: Dark brown body with gleaming golden-buff feathers on the crown and nape, and feathered legs down to the toes.

creatures.name: Peregrine-Bolt
creatures.habitat: Cliff Faces, River Gorges & Tall City Towers
creatures.education: The peregrine falcon is the fastest animal in the entire world! When diving in a hunting 'stoop' from high above, it reaches speeds over 240 miles per hour! It has specialized cone baffles inside its nostrils so it can breathe air at high speed.
creatures.exploration_trait: Stoop Blitz (Dives at supersonic speed to break brittle aerial crystal formations).
creatures.visual_notes: Blue-gray back with black helmet bars, barred white chest, and aerodynamic pointed wings.

creatures.name: Horned-Owl
creatures.education: Known as the 'tiger of the sky,' the great horned owl has almost no sense of smell—which is great because one of its favorite meals is skunks! Its feathered ear tufts are not actually ears; they are facial plumes used to signal moods and camouflage with tree bark.
creatures.exploration_trait: Silent Night Flight (Flies with zero acoustic footprint, avoiding disturbing nocturnal roosts).
creatures.visual_notes: Mottled brown-and-white barred feathers with prominent upright ear tufts and piercing golden eyes.

creatures.name: Barn-Ghost
creatures.habitat: Old Barns, Grasslands & Farm Meadow Margins
creatures.education: Barn owls have a heart-shaped facial disc that acts like a satellite dish, funneling the faintest sounds straight into their asymmetrical ears. Their hearing is so precise they can catch a mouse running under two feet of snow in pitch-black darkness!
creatures.exploration_trait: Acoustic Pinpoint (Pinpoints the exact location of burrowing critters beneath snow or thick grass).
creatures.visual_notes: Porcelain-white heart-shaped face with warm honey-buff and grey plumage sprinkled with pearl dots.

creatures.name: Raven-Lore
creatures.habitat: Boreal Forests, Mountains, Deserts & Coastal Cliffs
creatures.education: Ravens are among the smartest animals on Earth! They can solve multi-step logic puzzles, make and use tools, imitate human speech, and even roll down snowy hills just for fun! In the wild, ravens call wolves to carcasses so the wolves open the hide for them.
creatures.exploration_trait: Wolf Whisperer (Befriends wild wolves, reducing their agro radius and guiding them to food).
creatures.visual_notes: Massive glossy black raven with shaggy throat hackles, wedge-shaped tail, and wise intelligent black eyes.

creatures.name: Blue-Jay
creatures.education: Blue jays are the arborists of North American forests! A single blue jay can hide over 3,000 acorns in a single autumn. They forget where they buried many of them, which sprout into oak forests! They can also imitate hawk screams to scare other birds away from feeders.
creatures.exploration_trait: Acorn Cache (Recovers buried nuts and acorns that restore stamina during long journeys).
creatures.visual_notes: Vibrant cobalt-blue wings and tail barred in black, white chest, and expressive jaunty crest.

creatures.name: Gobble-Strut
creatures.diet: Acorns, Hickory Nuts, Seeds, Wild Berries
creatures.education: Wild turkeys can run at 25 miles per hour and fly at 55 miles per hour! The fleshy growth on a male turkey's forehead is called a 'snood,' which changes color from red to blue to white depending on how excited the turkey is.
creatures.exploration_trait: Mast Finder (Locates forest trees dropping heavy crops of nutritious acorns and nuts).
creatures.visual_notes: Iridescent bronze and copper plumage with fan-like tail display and colorful fleshy head snood.

creatures.name: Roadrunner
creatures.education: The greater roadrunner can sprint at over 20 miles per hour across burning desert gravel! They have a specialized black skin patch on their back that they expose to the morning sun like a solar panel to warm up quickly on freezing desert mornings.
creatures.exploration_trait: Desert Solar Warmth (Prevents nighttime cold penalties by soaking up early morning desert sunlight).
creatures.visual_notes: Streaked tan-and-brown plumage with shaggy crest, long balancing tail, and blue-and-red bare eye skin.

creatures.name: Ruby-Hummer
creatures.education: The ruby-throated hummingbird weighs less than a penny! Despite their tiny size, they fly non-stop for 20 hours across 500 miles of the open Gulf of Mexico without stopping during migration! Their wings beat 53 times per second.
creatures.exploration_trait: Hover Sip (Harvests delicate flower nectar from blossoms dangling over sheer cliff drops).
creatures.visual_notes: Glittering metallic emerald-green back with a throat gorget that flashes blazing ruby red in direct sun.

creatures.name: Sandhill-Bugle
creatures.habitat: Prairie Wet Meadows, Bogs & River Valleys
creatures.education: Sandhill cranes are one of the oldest living bird species, with fossils dating back over 2.5 million years! They have long coiled windpipes that produce a prehistoric bugling trumpet call that carries for over two miles across open prairies.
creatures.exploration_trait: Bugle Beacon (Summons lost mounts and distant party companions back to camp).
creatures.visual_notes: Stately tall slate-gray crane with a bright crimson crown patch and bustling tail plumes.

creatures.name: Blue-Heron
creatures.education: The great blue heron stands nearly four feet tall with a six-foot wingspan, but weighs only five to six pounds thanks to delicate hollow bones! It has specialized serrated middle claws that it uses like a comb to groom powder-down feathers.
creatures.exploration_trait: Stilt Wader (Wades through knee-deep river channels without alerting swimming fish).
creatures.visual_notes: Majestic blue-gray plumage with white crown, black plume crest, and dagger-like yellow bill.

creatures.name: Osprey-Fish
creatures.habitat: Rivers, Coastal Bays, Estuaries & Salt Marshes
creatures.education: Ospreys are master fishermen! They dive feet-first into water, sometimes submerging completely. They have barbed pads on their talons to hold slippery fish and can rotate their outer toe backward to carry captured fish head-first for aerodynamic flying!
creatures.exploration_trait: Aerodynamic Fish Carry (Transports aquatic catch and delicate water supplies without dropping them).
creatures.visual_notes: Dark brown back with pure white breast, dark eye bandit mask, and reversible outer talons.

creatures.name: Pileated-Peck
creatures.education: The pileated woodpecker is nearly the size of a crow! It chisels rectangular holes into dead trees to catch carpenter ants. Its tongue wraps all the way around its skull to cushion its brain against the force of hammering into solid wood at 20 times per second!
creatures.exploration_trait: Hardwood Chisel (Chips open dead tree snags to reveal hidden wood resin and carpenter ant hives).
creatures.visual_notes: Crow-sized black woodpecker crowned with a flamboyant flame-red crest and bold white neck stripes.

creatures.name: Cali-Condor
creatures.habitat: Rocky Coastal Gorges, Canyons & Redwood Cliffs
creatures.diet: Carrion of Deer, Elk, Cattle, Whales
creatures.education: The California condor has the largest wingspan of any bird in North America (nearly 10 feet)! In 1987, only 22 condors were left in the world. Thanks to historic breeding programs, they were saved from extinction and now soar wild over the Grand Canyon once more!
creatures.exploration_trait: Ancient Thermal (Soars indefinitely across massive canyon valleys without losing altitude).
creatures.visual_notes: Colossal black wings with white triangular wing linings, bare orange-pink head, and feathered ruff collar.

creatures.name: Snow-Goose
creatures.education: Snow geese fly in massive flocks of tens of thousands of birds in giant shifting 'V' formations! Their serrated black bills look like grinning grins with cutting teeth that can pull tough wetland roots right out of frozen tundra mud.
creatures.exploration_trait: Flock Formation (Provides slipstream drag reduction for all companions traveling together).
creatures.visual_notes: Pure snow-white plumage with jet-black wingtips, pink bill with black 'grinning patch,' and pink legs.

creatures.name: Wood-Drake
creatures.habitat: Swamp Creeks, Flooded Bottomlands & Beaver Ponds
creatures.education: The wood duck is one of the few duck species with sharp claws on its webbed feet, allowing it to perch comfortably in high oak trees! Baby ducklings jump from tree cavity nests over 50 feet up in the air down into soft leaf litter without getting hurt at all!
creatures.exploration_trait: Treetop Roost (Enables safe waterbird roosting in flooded forest tree crowns).
creatures.visual_notes: Spectacular rainbow-colored plumage with iridescent green crest, burgundy breast, and gold flanks.

creatures.name: King-Fisher
creatures.education: The belted kingfisher digs long nesting tunnels up to eight feet deep into muddy riverbanks! They have two foveae (visual focus spots) in each eye, allowing them to see clearly both in the air and through refracted water surfaces to spear fish.
creatures.exploration_trait: Refraction Piercer (Spears underwater fish from high aerial branches with 100% accuracy).
creatures.visual_notes: Stocky powder-blue bird with shaggy double crest, broad white collar, rust belly band, and dagger bill.

creatures.name: Magpie-Chat
creatures.diet: Insects, Berries, Grain, Carrion, Shiny Trinkets
creatures.education: Magpies are one of the only non-mammal animals that can recognize their own reflection in a mirror! They build domed rooftop stick nests the size of laundry baskets with two entrances so they always have an escape route if a hawk enters.
creatures.exploration_trait: Shiny Hoarder (Uncovers hidden shiny coins, silver trinkets, and buried metallic relics).
creatures.visual_notes: Long-tailed pied bird with velvety black head, snow-white belly, and iridescent emerald-blue wing sheens.

creatures.name: Whooper-Crane
creatures.habitat: Coastal Salt Marshes & Northern Boreal Bogs
creatures.education: The whooping crane is the tallest flying bird in North America, standing five feet tall! In 1941, only 15 cranes remained. Biologists used ultralight aircraft wearing white bird suits to guide young cranes along their historic migration routes to save the species!
creatures.exploration_trait: Ultralight Guide (Guides flocks of companions along secure sky corridors free of airborne hazards).
creatures.visual_notes: Towering snowy-white crane with jet-black wingtips, red bare crown patch, and majestic wingspan.

creatures.name: Castor-Dam
creatures.diet: Aspen, Willow & Birch Bark, Aquatic Lilies
creatures.education: Beavers have orange teeth because their enamel is reinforced with real iron to make them strong enough to fell huge trees! They build complex wooden dams that create wetlands, storing water and creating homes for thousands of species. Their flat tail slaps water to sound alarms!
creatures.exploration_trait: Dam Engineer (Builds log bridges across rushing rivers and floods dry ditches to create navigable canals).
creatures.visual_notes: Stout waterproof brown mammal with bright orange chisel teeth, webbed hind feet, and leathery paddle tail.

creatures.name: Bandit-Paw
creatures.diet: Crayfish, Berries, Nuts, Sweetcorn, Camp Scraps
creatures.education: Raccoons have ultra-sensitive front paws that get even more sensitive when wet! They can open complicated door latches, untie knots, and memorize puzzle solutions for over three years! Their black bandit mask reduces glare and helps them see at night.
creatures.exploration_trait: Master Lockpicker (Picks primitive door latches, chest padlocks, and disables wire traps).
creatures.visual_notes: Plump grizzled grey fur with a black bandit eye mask and five-ringed bushy tail.

creatures.name: Skunk-Spritz
creatures.diet: Insects, Grubs, Mice, Wild Fruit, Bird Eggs
creatures.education: Before spraying, a skunk always gives fair warning: it stamps its front feet, hisses, and does an athletic handstand! Its spray contains sulfur compounds that can be smelled over a mile away and can temporarily blind a predator.
creatures.exploration_trait: Musk Deterrent (Creates a safe perimeter around camps that apex predators refuse to approach).
creatures.visual_notes: Glossy black fur split by two bold snowy-white stripes running to a luxuriant plumed tail.

creatures.name: Opossum-Play
creatures.education: The opossum is North America's ONLY native marsupial (mothers carry babies in a belly pouch)! They have 50 teeth (more than any land mammal), immune systems resistant to snake venom, and when frightened, they involuntarily faint into a catatonic coma ('playing possum')!
creatures.exploration_trait: Tick Vaccum (Cleans party mounts of ticks and parasites, granting resistance to wilderness illnesses).
creatures.visual_notes: Scruffy silver-white fur, pink pointed snout, prehensile pink tail, and black leathery ears.

creatures.name: Kelp-Otter
creatures.education: Sea otters have the densest fur of any animal—up to one million hairs per square inch! They float on their backs in kelp forests, wrapping kelp around themselves like a sleeping bag so they don't drift away, and use smooth stones on their bellies as anvils to crack open shellfish!
creatures.exploration_trait: Anvil Toolmaker (Uses smooth river stones to crack open tough mineral geodes and rare clams).
creatures.visual_notes: Dense chocolate-brown fur with silvery-white face whiskers, floating happily on its back with an anvil stone.

creatures.name: River-Glider
creatures.education: River otters love having fun! They build natural mud and snow slides on riverbanks and slide down on their bellies just for the joy of it. They can swim at eight miles per hour and close their ears and nostrils underwater with specialized muscular valves.
creatures.exploration_trait: Belly Slide (Enables fast downhill toboggan sliding across mud and snow banks).
creatures.visual_notes: Sleek muscular chocolate coat, pale throat bib, webbed paws, and powerful tapering rudder tail.

creatures.name: Quill-Pine
creatures.diet: Tree Inner Bark (Cambium), Pine Needles, Leaves
creatures.education: A single porcupine has over 30,000 barbed quills! The quills have microscopic backward-facing scales that make them work like fishhooks: once embedded, normal muscle movements pull them deeper. The quills are coated in natural antibiotics to prevent accidental self-injury!
creatures.exploration_trait: Antibiotic Quill (Provides sterile needles and quills for suturing wounds and making compass needles).
creatures.visual_notes: Chunky dark brown mammal bristling with long white-tipped defensive quills and a heavy quilled tail.

creatures.name: Bobcat-Tuft
creatures.education: Named for its short 'bobbed' tail, the bobcat is an adaptable master stalker! Its soft fur-lined paws make zero sound when walking on dry leaves, and it can leap 10 feet horizontally to land directly onto a fleeing rabbit.
creatures.exploration_trait: Soft-Pad Stride (Nullifies footsteps sound completely, granting stealth even on crunchy dry surfaces).
creatures.visual_notes: Tawny-brown coat spotted in dark brown, ruffed cheek fur, tufted ears, and a black-tipped short tail.

creatures.name: Lynx-Snowshoe
creatures.education: The Canada lynx has giant snowshoe paws! Its enormous feet are covered in thick woolly fur and splay wide to act like natural snowshoes, allowing this stealthy cat to run on top of deep powdery snow where other predators sink and struggle.
creatures.exploration_trait: Snowshoe Tread (Walks over deep snow drifts and fragile ice bridges without breaking through).
creatures.visual_notes: Thick silver-grey winter fleece, long black ear tufts, large round furry snowshoe paws, and black tail tip.

creatures.name: Red-Vulpine
creatures.education: Red foxes use Earth's magnetic field to hunt! When hunting mice hidden under deep snow, they leap high into the air in a parabolic dive, aligning their jump with the planet's magnetic north. When aligned to the north, their pounces succeed 73% of the time!
creatures.exploration_trait: Magnetic Pounce (Detects buried metal trinkets and underground burrowing rodents through magnetic sense).
creatures.visual_notes: Flame-red coat, black stockings on legs, white throat bib, and a luxuriant white-tipped bushy brush tail.

creatures.name: Swift-Dune
creatures.education: The swift fox is the smallest wild dog in North America—about the size of a domestic housecat! It earned its name by running at speeds over 30 miles per hour in zig-zag evasion patterns across open prairie to escape eagles and coyotes.
creatures.exploration_trait: Prairie Evasion (Grants evasion agility boosts that help the player dodge charging territorial monsters).
creatures.visual_notes: Compact sandy-buff fox with black patches on its muzzle and a black-tipped bushy brush tail.

creatures.name: Coyote-Song
creatures.education: The coyote's scientific name means 'barking dog'! Coyotes are the most vocal mammals in North America, with 11 distinct vocalizations. When two coyotes howl in harmony, their shifting pitches create an acoustic auditory illusion making them sound like an entire pack of ten!
creatures.exploration_trait: Acoustic Mirage (Howls to create auditory decoys that lure predators away from homestead gates).
creatures.visual_notes: Grizzled grayish-tawny coat, slender pointed muzzle, bushy drooping tail, and golden intelligent eyes.

creatures.name: Ringtail-Cat
creatures.education: The ringtail isn't a cat—it is a relative of the raccoon! Early gold miners kept ringtails in their cabins because they were friendly and caught mice (earning them the nickname 'miner's cat'). Their back ankles can rotate 180 degrees, letting them scale sheer canyon walls!
creatures.exploration_trait: Miner's Lantern (Accompanies the player into mineshafts, keeping pests away and detecting toxic gas).
creatures.visual_notes: Sleek fawn body with enormous eyes, fox-like face, and a magnificent tail banded in black and white rings.

creatures.name: Prairie-Town
creatures.education: Prairie dogs have the most complex animal language ever decoded! They have distinct chirps that describe a predator's species, size, shape, color of clothing, and speed of approach! They live in vast underground 'towns' divided into organized neighborhoods.
creatures.exploration_trait: Town Lookout (Provides an advanced alarm system alerting the player to oncoming wandering bosses).
creatures.visual_notes: Chubby sandy-tan ground squirrel with a black-tipped tail, expressive paws, and watchful posture.

creatures.name: Glider-Pelt
creatures.diet: Acorns, Nuts, Fungi, Berries, Bird Eggs
creatures.education: Flying squirrels don't fly—they glide! They have a furry parachute membrane called a 'patagium' that stretches between their wrists and ankles. Under UV blacklight, their fur glows bright bubblegum pink! They use their flat tail as a steering rudder.
creatures.exploration_trait: Pink Parachute (Deploys a glider parachute allowing the player to glide gently down from tall cliffs).
creatures.visual_notes: Soft silky grey-brown fur, giant soulful dark eyes, and a furry gliding flap that glows hot pink under UV.

creatures.name: Badger-Digger
creatures.education: The American badger has shovel-like front claws so powerful it can dig straight down through hard prairie sod and completely vanish underground in less than a minute! Badgers famously form cooperative hunting partnerships with wild coyotes to hunt prairie dogs!
creatures.exploration_trait: Rapid Excavation (Can dig instant escape trenches to dodge dangerous area-of-effect monster attacks).
creatures.visual_notes: Flat wide muscular body with grizzled silver fur, white facial stripe, and formidable curved shovel claws.

creatures.name: Hare-Snowshoe
creatures.diet: Grass, Ferns, Birch Twigs, Willow Bark
creatures.education: The snowshoe hare is a master of seasonal color change! In summer, its coat is rusty brown to blend with forest soil. As days shorten in autumn, it molts into pure snowy-white fur to hide in winter snowdrifts! Its oversized furry hind feet prevent sinking into snow.
creatures.exploration_trait: Winter Shift (Camouflages according to seasonal ground conditions to prevent enemy ambushes).
creatures.visual_notes: Pure snow-white fluffy fur with black ear tips in winter, transforming into warm rusty brown in summer.

creatures.name: Ferret-Blackfoot
creatures.education: Once thought to be completely extinct, a tiny population of black-footed ferrets was rediscovered by a ranch dog in Wyoming in 1981! They are nocturnal masked hunters that slide through underground prairie dog burrows like flexible furry ribbons.
creatures.exploration_trait: Burrow Scout (Navigates narrow underground tunnel networks to scout monster positions).
creatures.visual_notes: Slender creamy-buff body with black feet, black tail tip, and an adorable raccoon-like black mask.

creatures.name: Musk-Lodge
creatures.education: Muskrats build mini-lodges made of cattails and marsh reeds called 'push-ups' that provide warm resting domes on winter ice! Their vertically flattened tails act like rudders, and they can hold their breath underwater for up to 15 minutes.
creatures.exploration_trait: Cattail Masonry (Gathers flexible marsh reeds used to weave insulating lodge mats and baskets).
creatures.visual_notes: Plump waterproof brown rodent with vertically flattened scaly tail and webbed hind feet.

creatures.name: Wolverine-Grit
creatures.habitat: Boreal Forests, Subarctic Taiga & Alpine Tundra
creatures.education: The wolverine is the ultimate pound-for-pound powerhouse of the north! Nicknamed the 'glutton' or 'skunk bear,' a 35-pound wolverine has been documented driving adult grizzly bears and entire wolf packs away from carcasses through pure ferocious grit!
creatures.exploration_trait: Gluttonous Defiance (Grants absolute resistance to terror, intimidation, and stagger effects).
creatures.visual_notes: Stocky muscular bear-like weasel with dense frost-resistant dark brown fur and two tawny side stripes.

creatures.name: Thunderhoof
creatures.education: The American bison is the national mammal of the United States! Weighing over 2,000 pounds, a bison can jump six feet vertically over fences and sprint at 35 miles per hour! When winter blizzards strike, bison turn their faces into the wind and walk directly through the storm.
creatures.exploration_trait: Blizzard Stride (Can plow through deep snowbanks and gale-force blizzards without slowing down).
creatures.visual_notes: Colossal woolly dark brown bovine with massive shoulder hump, bearded chin, and curved black horns.

creatures.name: Bouldear
creatures.habitat: Rocky Mountains, River Valleys & Alpine Meadows
creatures.diet: Salmon, Berries, Roots, Moths, Elk Calves
creatures.education: Grizzly bears have a prominent muscular hump between their shoulders that acts like a biological bulldozer engine, powering their long curved front claws to excavate rocky dens and rip apart rotten logs! Their sense of smell is seven times sharper than a bloodhound's.
creatures.exploration_trait: Boulder Roll (Can push massive granite boulders out of cave openings to unlock hidden caverns).
creatures.visual_notes: Towering shaggy brown bear with silver-tipped 'grizzled' fur, distinctive shoulder hump, and long digging claws.

creatures.name: Kodiak-Titan
creatures.education: The Kodiak bear is the largest bear in the world alongside the polar bear, standing over 10 feet tall when upright on its hind legs and weighing over 1,500 pounds! Living on isolated Alaskan islands with abundant salmon streams, they grow to titanic proportions.
creatures.exploration_trait: Salmon Surge (Attracts legendary prize salmon runs to fishing spots at river mouths).
creatures.visual_notes: Colossal golden-brown bear of monolithic stature with immense paws and thick waterproof fur.

creatures.name: Black-Ursus
creatures.diet: Berries, Acorns, Insects, Honey, Wild Roots
creatures.education: Black bears aren't always black! Depending on where they live, they can be cinnamon-brown, blonde, silver-blue (glacier bears), or even pure white (spirit bears of British Columbia)! Their curved claws make them expert tree climbers.
creatures.exploration_trait: Tree Scale (Can scramble up massive ancient trees to scout vantage points or harvest honey).
creatures.visual_notes: Agile rounded black bear with a tan muzzle, curved climbing claws, and curious expressive face.

creatures.name: Bull-Moose
creatures.habitat: Boreal Forest Lakes, Willow Bogs & River Valleys
creatures.diet: Aquatic Water Lilies, Willow & Birch Twigs
creatures.education: The moose is the tallest mammal in North America! Bull moose grow palmate antlers spanning six feet wide that they shed and regrow every single year. They are phenomenal swimmers that can dive over 18 feet deep underwater to feast on delicious water lily roots!
creatures.exploration_trait: Bog Strider (Tall ground mount that strides effortlessly through deep peat bogs and flooded rivers).
creatures.visual_notes: Towering dark brown cervid with a long Roman nose, throat dewlap 'bell,' and massive flattened palmate antlers.

creatures.name: Wapiti-Crown
creatures.habitat: Mountain Meadows, Aspen Groves & Conifer Forests
creatures.diet: Grasses, Forbs, Aspen Bark, Shrub Twigs
creatures.education: During autumn mating season, bull elk make an unforgettable, haunting vocalization called a 'bugle'—a high-pitched whistling cry that echoes across mountain valleys for miles! Native Americans called them 'Wapiti,' meaning 'white rump.'
creatures.exploration_trait: Bugle Clarion (Frees companions from confusion and fear status effects with an inspiring bugle call).
creatures.visual_notes: Noble light brown stag with dark chestnut mane neck ruff, ivory eye rings, and sweeping branched antlers.

creatures.name: Caribou-Trek
creatures.education: Caribou are the only deer species where BOTH males and females grow antlers! Their hooves change shape with the seasons: in summer, their footpads are spongy for wet tundra; in winter, the sponge shrinks and the hoof rims harden to cut through blue ice!
creatures.exploration_trait: Ice Cleat (Traverses slick glazed ice sheets without slipping or losing balance).
creatures.visual_notes: Dense grayish-brown fleece coat with snow-white neck mane and magnificent forward-sweeping antler tines.

creatures.name: Timber-Wolf
creatures.education: Wolves live in close family units led by cooperative breeding pairs! When wolves returned to Yellowstone National Park in 1995, they changed the behavior of deer, which allowed river willows to regrow, bringing back beavers and songbirds—a miracle called a 'trophic cascade'!
creatures.exploration_trait: Trophic Harmony (Restores ecological balance to depleted wilderness regions, boosting rare spawns).
creatures.visual_notes: Athletic grizzled gray-and-charcoal wolf with deep chest, thick brush tail, and piercing amber eyes.

creatures.name: Mountain-Cougar
creatures.diet: Mule Deer, Bighorn Sheep, Elk Calves
creatures.education: The cougar is the second-heaviest cat in the Americas after the jaguar. Because it cannot roar like a lion, it communicates through purrs, growls, and an eerie human-like scream! A cougar can leap 15 feet vertically up onto a cliff ledge from a standstill.
creatures.exploration_trait: Cliff Pounce (Can leap vertically onto high canyon rims that lack walking paths).
creatures.visual_notes: Sleek tawny-gray coat with white belly, dark muzzle whiskers, long tail, and calculating hazel eyes.

creatures.name: Bighorn-Clash
creatures.habitat: Alpine Meadows, Grassy Mountain Slopes & Cliffs
creatures.education: Male bighorn sheep engage in epic head-butting duels! Charging at 20 miles per hour, their horns collide with a sound like a rifle shot that echoes for miles across the mountains. Their skulls have two layers of bone and bubble-wrap fluid to prevent concussions!
creatures.exploration_trait: Headbutt Wall (Shatters cracked stone barricades blocking mountain tunnel entrances).
creatures.visual_notes: Sturdy muscular gray-brown ram with massive curled spiral horns and a bright white rump patch.

creatures.name: Mountain-Billy
creatures.education: Mountain goats are not true goats—they are rock-climbing antelopes! Their hooves have hard outer rims with soft, spongy rubber pads in the center that grip polished granite cliffs. They can jump 12 feet across cliff faces on cliffs so steep that not even wolves can follow them.
creatures.exploration_trait: Sheer Wall Stride (Scales 85-degree vertical rock faces without slipping).
creatures.visual_notes: Pure snow-white woolly coat with black backward-curved dagger horns, black beard, and nimble hooves.

creatures.name: Pronghorn-Flash
creatures.education: The pronghorn is the fastest land animal in the western hemisphere, capable of sprinting at 55 miles per hour and sustaining 35 mph for miles! They evolved this blistering speed to outrun the extinct American cheetah thousands of years ago.
creatures.exploration_trait: Hyper-Speed Mount (The fastest sustained overland ground mount across flat grassland plains).
creatures.visual_notes: Slender athletic reddish-tan runner with white neck stripes, dark pronged horns, and flashing white rump.

creatures.name: Whitetail-Flag
creatures.diet: Acorns, Twigs, Green Shoots, Farm Greens
creatures.education: When startled, the white-tailed deer raises its broad tail like a shining white flag! This signal warns other deer in the herd of danger while also showing the predator that it has been spotted, discouraging a useless chase.
creatures.exploration_trait: Flag Warning (Warns nearby allies of incoming hostile threats, increasing party defense).
creatures.visual_notes: Graceful reddish-brown deer with slender branched antlers and an eye-catching snowy-white tail flag.

creatures.name: Muley-Bound
creatures.habitat: Chaparral Foothills, Sage Scrub & Mountain Forests
creatures.diet: Shrub Twigs, Conifer Needles, Sagebrush, Forbs
creatures.education: Named for its oversized mule-like ears, the mule deer escapes predators by 'stotting'—bouncing with all four hooves hitting and leaving the ground together! This pogo-stick bounce lets them leap right over sagebrush and rocky obstacles that trip up running predators.
creatures.exploration_trait: Stotting Vault (Bounces cleanly over brush barriers, low boulder fields, and fences).
creatures.visual_notes: Sturdy gray-brown deer with huge furry ears, bifurcated fork antlers, and a black-tipped rope tail.

creatures.name: Everglades-Titan
creatures.habitat: Ancient Cypress Cathedrals of the Deep Everglades
creatures.diet: Wild Boars, Pythons, Deep Marsh Prey
creatures.education: Elder alligator bulls that thrive in protected national parks can reach 14 feet in length! These ancient wetland patriarchs maintain deep water trails used by generations of river creatures, anchoring the health of the entire river of grass.
creatures.exploration_trait: Cypress Chasm Ferry (Ferries large homestead expeditions across impassable deep swamp channels).
creatures.visual_notes: Enormous moss-covered black armored alligator with heavy scuted ridges and terrifying wide jaws.

creatures.name: Manatee-Gentle
creatures.habitat: Warm Coastal Springs, Estuaries & Shallow Rivers
creatures.education: Manatees are known as 'sea cows' because they graze peacefully on aquatic seagrass beds for eight hours a day! In winter, they congregate in warm crystal-clear freshwater springs that stay at 72°F year-round. Their closest land relatives are elephants!
creatures.exploration_trait: Warm Spring Spa (Heals fatigue, hypothermia, and environmental debuffs for all resting companions).
creatures.visual_notes: Plump friendly slate-gray gentle giant with paddle flippers and wrinkled whiskered split snout.

creatures.name: Beluga-Canary
creatures.education: Belugas are nicknamed the 'sea canaries' because of their chirping, whistling vocal songs that sailors could hear through the wooden hulls of ships! They have no dorsal fin (so they don't hit sea ice) and can change the shape of their forehead melon to focus echolocation!
creatures.exploration_trait: Ice-Bore Chime (Emits focused soundwaves that reveal breathing holes beneath sea ice).
creatures.visual_notes: Snow-white friendly whale with flexible smiling neck, round forehead melon, and no dorsal fin.

creatures.name: Bowhead-Ancient
creatures.education: The bowhead whale can live for over 200 years—the longest-lived mammal on planet Earth! They have enormous arched bow heads with thick bony skulls that they use like battering rams to break upward through two feet of solid sea ice to breathe!
creatures.exploration_trait: Icebreaker Ram (Breaks through thick frozen pack ice to forge navigable sea channels).
creatures.visual_notes: Colossal dark blue-black whale with a distinct white chin patch and massive triangular bow-shaped head.

creatures.name: Orca-Matriarch
creatures.habitat: Salish Sea & Pacific Northwest Coastal Inlets
creatures.education: Orcas are actually the largest dolphins on Earth! Pods are led by wise grandmothers who know the location of salmon runs during drought years. Each pod has its own unique vocal dialect of whistles and clicks passed down through generations like a human language.
creatures.exploration_trait: Pod Dialect (Coordinates the actions of all active companions in aquatic exploration).
creatures.visual_notes: Striking graphic black and white whale with tall dorsal fin, white eye patch, and saddle marking.

creatures.name: Grand-Thunderbison
creatures.habitat: Heart of the Great American Plains
creatures.education: The elder bison patriarch is an iconic symbol of resilience and freedom. Indigenous nations revere the white or elder bison as a sacred guardian of truth, balance, and the renewal of nature across the great plains.
creatures.exploration_trait: Great Plains Harmony (Pacifies territorial prairie storms and blesses homestead pastures with bountiful grass).
creatures.visual_notes: Monumental elder bison with a silver-frosted woolly cape, massive scarred horns, and a deep majestic stride.
